title: Bridging AI and Emotion: Enhanced Models for Personal Finance Manager Applications
venue: International Journal of Computing and Digital Systems
tldr: Novel Financial Advisor Application integrating anomaly detection, predictive modeling, and sentiment analysis achieves 92% anomaly detection accuracy and reduces prediction errors by 25% through emotion-aware financial planning.
problem_and_motivation: Contemporary financial advisory platforms rely on static rule-based structures that ignore essential user behavior and emotional data needed to provide personalized recommendations. These applications function as simple data carriers without analyzing frequency, mood, or preferences crucial for timely financial assistance. The inability to process unstructured data from user inputs and transaction descriptions limits the provision of relevant products or services that users can handle emotionally.
approach: Developed Financial Advisor Application with .NET Core 6 backend integrating Python AI capabilities via TensorFlow and Keras.
Implemented anomaly detection using Isolation Forest, LOF, and One-Class SVM for identifying fraudulent transactions and unusual spending patterns.
Applied Transformer, TCN, and N-BEATS deep learning models for predictive financial forecasting based on historical transaction data.
Integrated sentiment analysis using BERT and GPT fine-tuned on financial corpus to classify user emotions from transaction descriptions.
Created merchant recommendation engine using collaborative filtering and MCC code analysis for personalized discount offers.
findings: num: Anomaly detection achieved 92% accuracy, 90% precision, 85% recall, and 0.93 ROC-AUC score.
num: MAPE improved from 10.5% to 7.8% (25% reduction in prediction error) when sentiment analysis was incorporated.
Transformer model with sentiment analysis showed best performance for capturing long-term dependencies in spending patterns.
num: Predictive accuracy achieved 88% alignment with actual user behavior within 90% confidence interval.
num: Traditional budgeting applications report 70-80% precision; proposed system achieves 90% precision for anomaly detection.
N-BEATS model excelled in decomposing time-series data into trend and seasonality components for detailed behavior analysis.
System successfully categorized users into emotional segments (Stressed, Adventurous, Health-Focused) for personalized recommendations.
Feedback loop mechanism enabled continuous model refinement through user verification of flagged transactions.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper presents a comprehensive Financial Advisor Application that advances personal finance management by integrating three AI capabilities: anomaly detection for security, predictive modeling for financial forecasting, and sentiment analysis for emotional understanding. The research demonstrates that incorporating user sentiment into financial models reduces prediction errors by 25%, establishing emotion as a critical factor in financial decision-making. By comparing Transformer, TCN, and N-BEATS architectures, the study provides empirical evidence for optimal model selection in financial time-series prediction. The application's modular architecture using .NET Core 6 with Python AI integration creates a scalable framework for extending financial advisory services.
directly_justifies: Anomaly detection achieves 92% accuracy with 0.93 ROC-AUC, significantly outperforming traditional 70-80% precision systems.
Sentiment analysis integration reduces MAPE from 10.5% to 7.8%, demonstrating 25% improvement in prediction accuracy.
Transformer model excels at capturing long-term dependencies in spending patterns when combined with emotional data.
N-BEATS model effectively decomposes time-series data into interpretable trend and seasonality components.
System processes real-time transactions and generates personalized merchant recommendations based on emotional segments.
limits: Generalization across diverse financial behaviors requires testing with broader demographics and spending patterns.
Deep learning models demand significant computational resources, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices.
User trust and adoption of AI-driven financial recommendations need further investigation.
Models primarily process structured and semi-structured data; unstructured data processing remains limited.
Real-world deployment challenges including data privacy, security vulnerabilities, and regulatory compliance not fully addressed.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned for relevance. Domains 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 received high relevance ratings as the paper directly develops a personal finance application addressing core concerns of these domains. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) is highly relevant for evaluating landscape and limitations of financial advisory platforms. Domain 5 (Behavioral Profiles) is highly relevant for sentiment-based user profiling. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) is highly relevant for core forecasting contributions. Domain 7 (Budgeting) is highly relevant for integrated budgeting features. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) is highly relevant for security implementation. Domains 1-3 were rejected as the study focuses on international (Lebanese) context rather than Filipino demographics. Domains 9-14 received medium or low relevance as they address tangential aspects like mobile design, privacy, or synthetic data generation not central to this work.
